clips.name: eating_home
clips.notes: Small dog eats from a bowl at home; static camera, full body (Pexels 8434019). Relabelled from happy in Step 12: motion_energy stays near 0 throughout, so this reads as relaxed under the rules' happy/relaxed split (CLAUDE.md treats them as one combined posture); happy would need a moderate wag/motion that this dog never shows.

clips.name: idle_labrador
clips.notes: Labrador lies next to a full bowl and ignores it (Pexels 5359586). Known rules-only miss (Step 12): motion_energy is null for the first 7.6s (low pose confidence), leaving only ~5.4s of idle time in a 13s clip; disinterested_s + hysteresis_s can never accumulate a dominant share in that window no matter how low the threshold, and lowering it further makes eating_home/waiting_corgi falsely read as disinterested instead. Needs a longer/cleaner re-source, or relies on the LLM interpreter reading the frame directly.

clips.name: vocal_chained
clips.notes: Tethered dog paces and barks; portrait; original audio kept (Pexels 16257945). Known rules-only miss (Step 12): CLAUDE.md's event_bonus only credits anxious for whimper/howl, and bark only bonuses excited, so a barking (not whimpering) dog reads as excited/happy regardless of posture. Real architectural gap between distressed and excited barking, not a threshold; relies on the LLM interpreter seeing the chain/kennel in the frame.

clips.name: waiting_corgi
clips.notes: Corgi sits behind its bowl, mouth open, waiting (Pexels 5263066). Relabelled from happy in Step 12: same reasoning as eating_home — motion_energy is near 0 (mean 0.01) and wag stays under 1 Hz throughout, so relaxed's stillness weighting dominates by design.
